title: Chicken Piccata
subtitle: Italian sautéed chicken with lemon, capers, and butter sauce
excerpt: Thin chicken cutlets sautéed until golden, then finished in a sharp, glossy sauce of lemon juice, capers, and butter. A ten-minute pan sauce that showcases how good simple Italian cooking can be.

recipe.sourceNotes: Piccata is an Italian-American preparation applied to thin slices of chicken or veal (scaloppine) sautéed and finished with a sauce made by deglazing the pan with lemon juice and white wine, then mounting butter into it. The word piccata in Italian is the past participle of piccare, meaning to lard or to sting, referring to the sharp, piquant nature of the sauce. The preparation was well established in Italian cooking by the nineteenth century and came to American restaurants with Italian immigration. The method is the same as veal piccata (its more prestigious Italian cousin) but uses chicken, which makes it more accessible and equally good.

content.text: The sauce is mounted with cold butter off the heat at the end: this creates an emulsified, glossy sauce rather than a greasy, split one. Add the butter one piece at a time and swirl rather than stir. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon but still be pourable.

items.preparation: use 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts; pounded to 1 cm thickness
cold; cut into cubes; for the sauce

content.text: Season the chicken cutlets and dust lightly in flour. Heat the olive oil and a knob of butter in a large frying pan over high heat. Sear the chicken for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and keep warm.
Pour away any excess fat. Add the white wine and let it bubble for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits. Add the stock and lemon juice. Boil for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.

Remove the pan from the heat. Add the cold butter cubes one at a time, swirling the pan between each addition until the sauce is glossy and emulsified. Add the capers and parsley. Taste and adjust the salt. Return the chicken and spoon the sauce over. Serve immediately.
